q: How many players from each team are on the field at the kickoff of a soccer match?
note: The goalkeeper is one of the eleven, and a match cannot continue if a side is reduced to fewer than seven players.

q: In soccer, which player is allowed to handle the ball inside their own penalty area?
note: The keeper is also the only player required to wear a colour that stands out from both teams and the officials.

q: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football?
note: Despite the name, the ball never has to touch the ground, which is a leftover from the sport's rugby ancestry.

q: What is the name of the National Football League's championship game?
note: The name was coined by an owner who had watched his children bouncing a toy called a Super Ball.

q: In soccer, what colour card does a referee show to send a player off the field?
note: An English referee came up with the yellow and red system after being stuck at a traffic light.

q: Which position in American football normally throws the ball to the receivers?
note: The name simply describes where he lines up behind the front line, alongside the half-back and full-back.

q: A standard soccer match is played as two halves of how many minutes each?
note: The clock never stops, so the referee adds stoppage time at the end of each half instead.

q: In soccer, what is the term for one player scoring three goals in a single match?
note: The phrase was borrowed from cricket, where a bowler who took three wickets in three balls was rewarded with a hat.

q: Which country hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup, in 1930?
note: They built a new stadium for the tournament and beat neighbours Argentina four goals to two in the final.

q: England won the men's soccer World Cup for the first time in which year?
note: They beat West Germany four goals to two after extra time at Wembley, on home soil.

q: How many points is a successful field goal worth in American football?
note: The same kick between the posts is worth only one point when taken straight after a touchdown.

q: How many yards separate the two goal lines on an American football field?
note: Adding the two end zones of ten yards each makes the painted field 120 yards long in total.

q: In American football, a team has four downs to advance the ball how many yards?
note: Making them resets the count, which is why commentators are forever saying first and ten.

q: What is the name of the governing body of world soccer, headquartered in Zurich?
note: It was founded in Paris in 1904 by seven European associations, none of them British.

q: Which soccer rule disallows a goal because the attacker was too far forward when the ball was played to them?
note: A player can never be caught by it from a throw-in, a corner or a goal kick.

q: What is the name of the trophy handed to the winners of the Super Bowl?
note: It is made of sterling silver by the jeweller Tiffany and shaped like a football standing on a tee.

q: In soccer, how many yards from the goal line is the penalty spot?
note: The penalty kick was introduced in 1891, and the goalkeeper must keep part of one foot on the line until the ball is struck.

q: In American football, what is the name for a long, desperate pass thrown towards the end zone as time runs out?
note: The phrase caught on after a 1975 playoff game in which the winning quarterback said he threw it and said a prayer.

q: Super Bowls are traditionally identified by numbers written in which form?
note: The fiftieth game broke the habit and used the ordinary figure 50, because a lone letter L looked odd on the merchandise.

q: In American football, what is the two-point score called when a ball carrier is tackled in his own end zone?
note: It is the only score in the game worth two points on its own, and the scoring team gets the ball back afterwards.
